turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi Dr. Smith. I'm here because... well, I just can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations at work again and again. I end up staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves. Even when I know I already checked them, I just... I feel like I have to do it one more time. Because if I don't, I get this intense feeling that something bad is going to happen and it'll be my fault. It's just gotten really out of hand.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes excessive, repetitive checking of spreadsheets and calculations at work that lasts for hours even after knowing they were checked, driven by a need to prevent something bad from happening.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel the urge to recheck the spreadsheets, is it because a specific unwanted thought or image keeps popping into your mind that you can't shake off, or is it more that you feel things simply have to be done in a particular exact way to feel right?
turns.patient_response: It's definitely a specific thought. Even after I check and I know the numbers match, this thought just keeps jumping into my head that I missed one hidden mistake somewhere in payroll or the taxes. I start thinking that somebody's check won't go through, or that the firm will get in trouble. I try to push it away, but... it just comes right back. It's like I can't trust my own eyes anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes recurrent, intrusive, and unwanted thoughts of making mistakes that they unsuccessfully attempt to suppress, consistent with obsessions.
